Voice practice

ON THIS PAGE

The workspace's Voice practice tool is a small practice companion: an optional pitch meter, a session timer and a short form for how it went. What it adds to your journal is ordinary text, so you can also write the same thing by hand.

What happens to your voice. The microphone turns on only when you press Start pitch meter, and only after your browser asks your permission. The sound is analysed inside the page, a few times a second, to estimate its pitch. Nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere: no audio, and no stream of numbers. Stop, closing the dialog or leaving the page turns the microphone off, and the dialog says Microphone off. Your journal changes only when you press Add to this entry.

Using the pitch meter

  1. In Write, choose Voice practice in the Tools row.
  2. Press Start pitch meter and allow the microphone. Speak, hum or sing as you usually practise.
  3. The dialog shows the pitch right now, a strip of the last half minute, and the session's median (the middle value), low and high (the 10th and 90th percentiles, so a stray squeak or a cough barely moves them) and voiced time (how long it heard a clear pitch, not breaths or silence).
  4. Press Stop when you are done. You can start again; the measurements add up until you choose Clear measurements.

The meter reads roughly 60 to 500 Hz. It works best in a quiet room with one voice. Browsers' echo cancelling, noise suppression and automatic volume are turned off for the meter so they do not bend the sound. A screen reader hears the median every few seconds rather than every change.

Target range (optional). If you want one, enter a range in Hz; it is shown as a band behind the strip, and the current reading is coloured while it is inside. There is no default and no score: the range is yours to choose, change or leave empty. It is the only thing the tool remembers, in this browser only.

Session timer. Start and pause it whenever you like; it counts up, never down. The minutes come from it (or from how long the meter was on), and you can change them.

What gets added

Fill in what is useful, all optional: minutes, the exercise, resonance on your own 1–5 scale, strain (0 none to 5 a lot), how much it felt like you (1–5), and a note. Uncheck Include the measured pitch to keep the numbers out. Add to this entry writes it at the cursor, inside the day you are writing:

### 2026-10-27 | Tuesday

#### Voice practice

Pitch, measured on this device: median 182 Hz, most of the time between 160 and 205 Hz, over 2 min 05 s of voiced sound. No audio was recorded.

Easier after humming first.

Recording: [take-1.m4a](assets/take-1.m4a)

:::record measurement
metric: pitch-hz
unit: Hz
value: 182
low: 160
high: 205
:::

:::record measurement
metric: voice-minutes
unit: min
value: 12
:::

:::record observation
method: voice-practice@1
exercise: Sirens
resonance: 4
strain: 1
felt-like-me: 5
recording: assets/take-1.m4a
:::

The observation uses the field names of the voice-practice method, so notes written from its writing invitation line up with the tool's.

Charting progress

The numbers belong to the day they are in. A chart record draws them over time; this one shows the last few weeks:

:::record chart
metrics: pitch-hz, voice-minutes, felt-like-me
start: 2026-10-01
end: 2026-10-31
:::

Two notes for the same metric on one day are drawn as their average, so for a day's total minutes, add one note at the end of the day or change the first one's value:. Use Numbers .csv ↓ in the Tools row to take them to a spreadsheet.

Recordings you made elsewhere

The tool never records. If you recorded yourself with another app, choose Attach a recording ＋ in the dialog: the file is attached to this journal (it travels inside the .jotz when you download) and named in the note as recording:, with a link to it, when you press Add. Recordings already attached with Attach a file ＋ are in the list too.

Privacy, in short

  • No microphone access until you press Start; it ends on Stop, on closing the dialog and on leaving the page.
  • Sound is analysed in the page and dropped; no audio or measurements are kept, uploaded or sent.
  • Only your target range is remembered, in this browser. The journal holds only what you add.
